title: Spring simulations estimate velocity with a forward difference
evidence: In physics__spring__damping_regimes, frame 0 / 0 ms reports dx=30 for all Flutter regimes and 34.8282 (under), 34.6680 (critical), 34.3399 (over) in Incular. The direct scroll spring also reports 0 vs 4.9438 at frame 0. Position remains within tolerance.
impact: Spring consumers receive velocity from one millisecond ahead; the same value feeds completion checks and scroll handoffs.
cause: Incular estimates dx as (x(t + 1 ms) - x(t)) / 1 ms instead of using the closed-form derivative.
fix_direction: Use the analytic derivative for each damping regime in velocity and completion checks.

title: Negative acceleration marks gravity simulations done immediately
evidence: In physics__gravity__negative_acceleration_threshold, both positions are 0 with end=100 at frame 0. Flutter reports done=0 and Incular reports done=1.
impact: A negative-acceleration simulation starting below its positive threshold can be treated as finished before it moves.
cause: The Incular completion check compares position to the threshold based on acceleration sign rather than comparing absolute position to the threshold.
fix_direction: Use abs(position) >= end for either acceleration sign.

title: Bounded friction changes velocity and omits the bound-distance tolerance
evidence: In physics__bounded_friction__position_and_velocity, frame 3 / 48 ms has clamped x=4: Flutter dx=90.8356, Incular dx=0. In physics__bounded_friction__distance_tolerance, start=3.9995 is 0.0005 from max=4 under the 0.001 default distance tolerance; Flutter is done at frame 0, Incular is not, and at frame 1 Flutter dx=96.8468 while Incular dx=0.
impact: Consumers lose the inner friction velocity at a display bound, and a position already within Flutter's settling tolerance continues in Incular.
cause: Incular zeros velocity at bounds and tests exact raw-position crossing rather than distance from the clamped position to the bound.
fix_direction: Preserve the inner friction velocity and apply tolerance.distance to the clamped position when checking bounds.

title: Clamped simulations cannot clamp velocity
evidence: Source review; the diagnostic twin sets Flutter dxMax=50 while Incular has no equivalent option. Frame 0 reports Flutter 50 vs Incular 200; configurations are intentionally not equivalent.
impact: Callers cannot cap velocity independently from position as Flutter's ClampedSimulation allows.
cause: Incular's constructor stores only position bounds and forwards the inner velocity unchanged.
fix_direction: Add optional dxMin/dxMax bounds and clamp the forwarded velocity.

title: Completion comparisons are inclusive at Flutter's strict tolerance boundary
evidence: physics__friction__tolerance_boundary uses velocity=tolerance=0.001 and reports done=0 in Flutter vs 1 in Incular at frame 0. physics__spring__tolerance_boundary starts exactly one distance tolerance from equilibrium and reports done=0 vs 1 at frame 0.
impact: A simulation exactly on the tolerance edge can stop one evaluation earlier in Incular.
cause: Incular uses <= where Flutter uses strict comparisons through nearZero.
fix_direction: Use strict comparisons for friction velocity and spring distance/velocity tolerance checks.

title: Spring descriptions normalize inputs Flutter preserves
evidence: physics__spring_description__damping_regimes at frame 0: raw (mass=0, stiffness=0, damping=-1) remains unchanged in Flutter and becomes (1,100,10) in Incular. A damping ratio of -0.25 gives damping=-5/type=under in Flutter and damping=20/type=critical in Incular.
impact: The same parameters can select a different spring regime and produce different motion for unusual or invalid physical inputs.
cause: Incular adds default substitutions for invalid mass, stiffness, damping, and ratio that Flutter's constructors do not apply.
fix_direction: Preserve supplied values, or document the sanitization as an intentional API difference.

title: Duration and bounce spring creation retains sub-millisecond precision
evidence: physics__spring_description__duration_bounce passes 300500 µs and bounce=0.3. Flutter reports stiffness=438.6491, damping=29.3215, duration=300 ms; Incular computes stiffness=437.1906, damping=29.2727, and duration=301 ms from its spring fields.
impact: Sub-millisecond duration inputs produce different spring timing and damping.
cause: Incular converts full microsecond duration to fractional seconds while Flutter first truncates to whole milliseconds.
fix_direction: Use whole milliseconds before deriving stiffness when Flutter parity is intended.

title: SpringDescription duration and bounce getters are missing
evidence: Source review. The duration/bounce frame twin reads Flutter's getters and reconstructs the same formulas in test code because the Incular type has no equivalent accessors.
impact: Callers cannot query the perceptual duration or bounce of an existing spring description through Incular's public API.
cause: The Rust type exposes only the physical coefficients and constructors.
fix_direction: Add duration and bounce accessors with Flutter's derivation and rounding.

title: SpringSimulation lacks snapToEnd
evidence: Source review. Direct frame twins use Flutter's default snapToEnd=false; Incular has no equivalent configuration for the true case. Its ScrollSpringSimulation snaps position but leaves the inherited velocity unchanged.
impact: Callers cannot request Flutter's endpoint-and-zero-velocity behavior on a general spring simulation.
cause: Endpoint snapping is available only through a separate scroll wrapper, with position-only snapping.
fix_direction: Add a snap_to_end option that snaps both position and velocity after completion.

title: FrictionSimulation omits Flutter's desktop and endpoint helpers
evidence: Source review. The ordinary zero-constant-deceleration curve is frame-tested and matches; Flutter's constantDeceleration, through constructor, finalX, and timeAtX have no public counterpart on Incular's animation simulation.
impact: Callers cannot use Flutter's desktop constant-deceleration behavior or tune/query friction motion through endpoints using the Incular animation type.
cause: The animation crate implements only the basic exponential decay; similar through behavior is private to scroll ballistics.
fix_direction: Expose constant deceleration, a through constructor, final position, and time-at-position on the animation friction type.

title: Simulation tolerance is not available through the trait
evidence: Source review. Concrete Incular constructors may accept a tolerance, but generic simulation users cannot inspect or update a shared tolerance through the Simulation trait.
impact: Code that adjusts tolerance after construction or handles simulations through a base interface cannot be ported directly.
cause: The Rust trait exposes only the three time-sampled methods.
fix_direction: Expose tolerance through the simulation abstraction or document a builder-based equivalent.

title: nearEqual and nearZero have no public Incular equivalent
evidence: Source review; the inventory marked both helpers unresolved. Incular has only a private scroll-local near_zero helper.
impact: Callers cannot reuse Flutter's null-aware near-equality and near-zero checks from Incular's public physics API.
cause: The helper is local to scroll spring completion instead of a shared public utility.
fix_direction: Add public near_equal and near_zero functions if parity with Flutter's exported physics utilities is desired.
